citationText: Video Services Forum (VSF) Technical Recommendation TR-06-1, “Reliable Internet Stream Transport (RIST) Protocol Future Work Future studies that did not fit into the scope of this paper are: ■■ Jitter characteristics: Study the jitter characteristics that the different implementations add. Ideally, the pattern of interpacket gaps on the input of the sender should be recreated exactly on the output of the receiver. ■■ End-to-end latency: Another interesting area to study is the full end-to-end latency; this study has considered the situation where each protocol has an identically sized latency buffer. ■■ Congestion control: This study has not attempted to push the protocols to the limit with regard to congestion control, which is something that should be explored further. ■■ Quality of experience: As suggested earlier, studying the quality of experience instead of pure packet drop statistics is also very important. A different way to present the data in a study such as this one, albeit a more workintensive method, could be to decide on an acceptable rate of residual packet drops and to attempt to determine the boundaries in line drop rate that allows the protocols to stay within that acceptable residual drop rate. That is, what are the worst conditions that each protocol can be subjected to and still perform acceptably. Additionally, the measurements could be presented in the form of errored seconds instead, that is, a count of the number of seconds that contain any dropped packets. It may be that for two implementations with the same residual drop rate, one of them has the loss more grouped and thus has fewer errored seconds, which may lead to fewer visible artifacts. ■■ High-bandwidth ARQ transport: With cloud being leveraged also for high-end workflows, performing similar benchmarks with much greater bandwidths, such as a 3 Gb/s JPEG-XS compressed ultrahigh-definition (UHD) signal, would be of interest. In addition, as bandwidths grow well into the multiple of 10 Gb/s range, there are also performance aspects when it comes to the platform itself. For example, from a CPU/memory perspective, is there a tradeoff between ARQ and FEC for pure execution purposes at these high speeds? Conclusion In the last year alone, retransmission technology has gained a lot of attention, driven by both initiatives such as the SRT Alliance and RIST, but also as a consequence of the industry starting to realize the importance of the technology as cloud starts to cement itself further as a key part of the broadcast workflow. The two major open alternatives in the market, RIST and SRT, all have backing from a large number of vendors and broadcasters. But this is in a market that is already a decade in the making in terms of proprietary solutions and ecosystems. Therefore, while RIST and SRT are technically good alternatives already today, the large proprietary ecosystems already in place are likely to exist for many years, while being augmented by these new challengers.
